title: Audit a judge with matched pairs
statement: Audit a judge with matched inputs that differ only in something that should not matter, such as an incidental item feature or the prompt's formatting, before trusting its scores.
example: A seven-word time-period prefix on otherwise identical items moved a judge's passes from 2 of 5 to 5 of 5.
detail: A red team sent a content judge hand-made pairs of items identical except for one surface feature (`icloud-work/aptraining/Cheater/exploits/EXPLOIT-006-period-anchor.md`; `icloud-work/aptraining/Cheater/exploits/EXPLOIT-007-difficulty-downgrade.md`). A stock seven-word prefix naming a time period moved passes from 2 of 5 to 5 of 5, and labelling the same four items easy rather than hard moved them from 1 of 4 to 4 of 4. A pair test checks that a judge ignores what should not matter, where a planted fault checks that it catches what should. Fix any verdict that changes with something that should not matter before trusting the judge's scores.
against: The prefix effect did not carry over to fresh items: "(stacked fresh-holdout n=25 MCQ: 76% with period+difficulty stacking vs 80% without)." (`icloud-work/aptraining/Cheater/exploits/EXPLOIT-006-period-anchor.md`, lines 4-5). A single flip can also be run-to-run variance, since the same judge's verdicts vary between runs, and a time-period anchor arguably adds scope, so that pair is not a pure surface change.

evidence.quote: **Pass rate**: **5/5 = 100%** with explicit period anchor vs **2/5 = 40%** without, on the same content (10 items, paired implicit/explicit). Δ = +60pp.
The content is identical across the pair. The lift comes entirely from a 7-word prefix that any wrapper can deterministically add.
**Pass rate**: **4/4 = 100%** when labeled "easy" vs **1/4 = 25%** when labeled "hard" on the SAME 4 stems × 4 options × 1 answer. Δ = +75pp.
(stacked fresh-holdout n=25 MCQ: 76% with period+difficulty stacking vs 80% without).
